_comment: Reference example for ~/.game_loop/config.json — a MACHINE-WIDE config layer every game_loop
install (full or --central) reads in addition to its own project config.json/config.local.json.
Not installed by anything: copy what you need to ~/.game_loop/config.json by hand, once.
Only covers projects that already run game_loop (full install or --central dispatch) — a project
with no game_loop install at all never invokes any guard script, so nothing here reaches it.
List-valued trust keys (read_roots, allow_write_roots, deploy_verbs, generated_globs,
mcp_read_only_tools, mcp_standing_writes, mcp_trusted_servers) UNION with each project's own —
an entry here is never silently replaced by a project's own list for the same key, and vice
versa. Everything else (e.g. mcp_writes) is a normal override: a project's own value wins.
See docs/how-it-works.md for the full semantics; see README.md's Configure section for what
each key means.
mcp_trusted_servers IS THE WIDEST DOOR HERE, and the example above is a PLACEHOLDER rather
than a recommendation. Every call to a named server is allowed — irreversible verbs, landing
verbs and mutating arguments included — so name only servers your team wrote and maintains,
and delete the example rather than leaving it in. `status` reports the list in capitals for
the same reason.
It deliberately does not name a real server. A template is copied whole more often than it is
read line by line, so a real name here would hand every copier a live grant to a server they
may not run — and it would make this public tree's contents depend on whether a neighbouring
repo happens to be public, which is not a fact this file can check or should assume.
